o: We must cut `nums` into a non-empty strictly increasing prefix (left) and a non-empty strictly decreasing suffix (right), minimizing the absolute difference of their sums, or return -1 if no cut works. For `[1,3,2]`, cutting after index 1 gives left `[1,3]` (sum 4) and right `[2]` (sum 2), difference 2. For `[1,2,4,3]`, both valid cuts give difference 4. For `[3,1,2]` no cut satisfies both shapes, so -1. With n up to 1e5 we cannot recheck each cut in O(n); precomputing 'strictly increasing up to i' and 'strictly decreasing from i' flags plus prefix sums gives a linear scan.
k: A cut at index i is valid iff nums[0..i] is strictly increasing AND nums[i+1..n-1] is strictly decreasing.
Prefix sums let us evaluate |sum(left) - sum(right)| in O(1) per cut.
Both shapes are independent per side, so simple boolean sweeps suffice.

a.i: For every split point, directly verify the increasing/decreasing property by scanning both sides and compare sums. This is the natural first idea and is fine for tiny inputs.
s: Try every index i from 0 to n-2 as the last index of left.
Scan left to confirm strict increase, scan right to confirm strict decrease.
If valid, record |sum(left)-sum(right)| and return the minimum, or -1 if none.
a.t: O(n^2) - each of the n-1 cuts is validated and summed by a linear scan

a.i: inc[i] is true iff nums[0..i] is strictly increasing, dec[i] iff nums[i..n-1] is strictly decreasing; both follow by one-line recurrences. Then a cut after i is valid exactly when inc[i] && dec[i+1], and prefix sums give the difference instantly.
s: Build inc left-to-right and dec right-to-left with boolean recurrences.
Build prefix sums of the array.
For each cut i in [0, n-2], if inc[i] and dec[i+1], update the answer with |pre[i+1] - (total - pre[i+1])|.
a.t: O(n) - three linear passes over the array
a.sp: O(n) for the flag arrays (reducible to O(1))

w: Use Approach 2 in an interview; mention Approach 1 only as a stepping stone. Pitfalls: forgetting that both parts must be non-empty (loop i only to n-2), confusing non-decreasing with strictly increasing, and integer overflow of sums in Java/C++ (use 64-bit). Follow-ups: what if parts may be empty, or the split must maximize rather than minimize the difference?
